(hA.orthogonalFamily_eigenspace_inf_eigenspace hB).comp (f := fun c : Module.End.Eigenvalues B × Module.End.Eigenvalues A => (c.1.val, c.2.val))
  fun c d h => Prod.ext (Subtype.ext (congrArg Prod.fst h)) (Subtype.ext (congrArg Prod.snd h))
explanation: The library's `JointEigenSpace A B c` is defined as `eigenspace A c.2.val ⊓ eigenspace B c.1.val`. Mathlib's `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.orthogonalFamily_eigenspace_inf_eigenspace` says the family `i ↦ eigenspace A i.2 ⊓ eigenspace B i.1`, indexed by all of `𝕜 × 𝕜`, is an `OrthogonalFamily`. Taking `𝕜 = ℂ`, the theorem is the same family restricted to pairs of eigenvalues, through the injective map `c ↦ (c.1.val, c.2.val)`. That is the routine reindexing `OrthogonalFamily.comp hf`. The library's proof does exactly this, applying the Mathlib lemma at `hf.ne hij`. All of the mathematical content, the orthogonality of joint eigenspaces of symmetric operators, comes from the Mathlib lemma. I have not compiled the derivation. It assumes Lean unfolds `JointEigenSpace` when it checks the result against the goal, which should happen because it is a plain `def`.
